summary: This week brought fresh congressional interest after lawmakers viewed UAP footage that reportedly shifted at least one skeptic's perspective, while separate reporting raised questions about missing government personnel with ties to classified research and advanced physics work. Luis Elizondo continued making headlines with recollections of pressure he faced, neither confirming nor denying his role in past secrecy efforts, as attention also turned to the decades-old 1952 DC UFO encounter and efforts to surface missing recordings from that incident. The Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office released new authorization documents and technical assessments examining factors like satellite interference and visual parallax in UAP observations, while defense officials acknowledged the military remains largely stumped by repeated incursions over U.S. bases. The week also surfaced calls for stronger legal protections for whistleblowers facing retaliation, underscoring ongoing tensions between those pushing for transparency and what some researchers characterize as efforts to derail disclosure momentum.
